ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.20634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation asks one question at volume: does this evidence support this claim? The answer is one bit, yet most pipelines obtain it from a text generator and pay generation prices for the prose wrapped around it. We compare a non-generative decision model, which returns a typed value from a declared enumeration together with a native probability and no text, against a frontier LLM configured as an engineer would deploy it for binary classification. A component whose job is to catch unsupported claims should be judged on that rate, and the conventional headline hides it. Third, because the errors differ they compose: routing the claims the cheap model is confident about and escalating the rest reaches 74.10 at USD 2.92 per thousand claims against 73.83 at USD 8.93, with the threshold chosen out of fold. ai.title: MSP: Modality Self-Play for Training Multimodal LLMs Without Paired Cross-Modal Data
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.20965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large multimodal models have achieved remarkable progress by scaling model capacity and training on massive paired multimodal data. However, this paradigm introduces a fundamental bottleneck: aligned multimodal datasets are expensive to curate, difficult to scale across diverse modality combinations, and increasingly constrain further progress. We introduce Modality Self-Play (MSP), a training framework for multimodal foundation models based on proxy-mediated modality composition. Instead of relying on paired cross-modal data, MSP uses anchor-supporting proxy textual descriptions of unseen modalities as semantic bridges during training. Given an observed modality (e.g., image or audio), the model generates proxy descriptions for complementary unseen modalities, which are then encoded and aligned with the observed modality through learned bridges, enabling cross-modal interaction without real paired non-text supervision. Our central hypothesis is that proxy text, combined with contrastively trained pretrained encoders, provides sufficient semantic structure for multimodal composition to emerge. We show that MSP enables zero-shot modality composition: models trained only with a real anchor modality and accompanying proxy descriptions can integrate and reason over multiple modalities at inference time despite never observing real paired non-text data during training. ai.title: Rubric Judgments Lack Uncertainty: Conformal Weighting for LLM Evaluation
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.21214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rubric-based evaluation is widely used to assess large language model (LLM) outputs by decomposing quality into multiple criteria and assigning each a binary judgment from an LLM verifier. However, judgment certainty varies substantially across criteria. Existing methods uniformly aggregate these judgments into a final score, implicitly treating every criterion as equally certain and overlooking this heterogeneity. As a result, uncertain judgments remain incorporated into reward estimation without distinction, potentially yielding misleading training signals for downstream reinforcement learning (RL). To address this limitation, we propose Uncertainty-aware Rubric Weighting (URW), a training-free framework that quantifies criterion-level judgment uncertainty via conformal calibration. Specifically, URW elicits a soft uncertainty signal from a fixed pool of paraphrased judgment templates and converts it into a per-criterion weight using split-conformal $p$-values with provable coverage guarantees. Extensive experiments demonstrate that URW consistently improves pairwise preference accuracy and delivers stronger downstream RL alignment.

ai.title: Auditing Escalation Reliability in Healthcare LLM Agents: A Perturbation-Controlled Benchmark of Workflow-State Failures
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.21270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trustworthy biomedical AI requires reliable action selection when evidence is missing, stale, conflicting, or late, not only accurate answers on static inputs. We instantiate an episode-level evaluation protocol as 400 synthetic healthcare workflow episodes: 40 hand-authored semantic seeds across four task classes, two surface parameterizations, and five controlled variants, scored on ANSWER/ASK CLARIFICATION/ABSTAIN/ESCALATE under a pre-declared 5:1 missed-versus-unnecessary escalation cost. Reference actions are single-author study-policy labels, not clinician-adjudicated ground truth. Across five open-weight configurations (1.7B--9.7B), clean decision accuracy reaches 0.97, yet uncertainty-prompted models miss 32--97% of required escalations. The stronger 9.7B configuration narrows but does not remove the gap, falling from 0.97 clean accuracy to 0.78 under conflict. Verbalized confidence is inconsistent (ECE 0.10--0.54; failure AUROC 0.48--0.77), and a development-tuned confidence-only policy yields no utility gain. A transparent workflow-aware controller improves 5:1 utility for every model and reduces missed escalations to 0.12--0.24, at specificity 0.83--0.93. However, a 30-concept lexical stress test reduces each rule detector's recall from 1.00 on trigger phrases to 0.00 on unseen paraphrases, limiting the controller claim to this benchmark. ai.title: PremiseCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of Human and AI Peer Reviews
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.21046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Peer review is under strain from the growth of submissions, and review comments written by humans or AI can misstate what a paper says. We introduce ReviewFact, a benchmark that labels such factual errors in review comments under one definition across NLP, machine learning, and the natural sciences, and that measures cost and latency alongside accuracy. A frontier LLM checks comments well but must read the whole paper for each check, while cheap decision models, which score whether a statement holds in a text, fall far short on whole comments that mix several implicit assertions. PremiseCheck is a framework that combines the two. An LLM rewrites each comment as explicit premises without reading the paper, and a decision model checks each premise against the paper. When each comment is checked on its own, PremiseCheck reaches accuracy comparable to GPT-5.5 across all three fields at about half its cost, and on NLP reviews at a quarter of its cost and less than half its latency.
ai.summary: Peer review is under strain from the growth of submissions, and review comments written by humans or AI can misstate what a paper says.

ai.title: Beyond Retrieval Failure: Understanding Why LLMs Miss Evidence in Multi-Hop RAG
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.21184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) requires an agent to retrieve evidence for a sequence of dependent sub-questions. When a wrong answer lacks a required passage, the passage may be inaccessible to the retriever, or the agent may have failed to issue a query that would retrieve it. Standard retrieval evaluations conflate these two causes. We study how much apparent retrieval failure is instead caused by search drift: the search no longer tracks an unanswered sub-question. Holding the retriever, corpus, and generation model fixed, we introduce ExecutionRAG, a training-free requirement register that records open sub-questions and their supporting evidence. The register changes search guidance but not evidence access, so each gold passage it recovers certifies that the passage was reachable by the original retriever. On 1,000 MuSiQue questions, the number of wrong answers with unretrieved required evidence falls from 382 to 234 with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and from 383 to 274 with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B. These counts correspond to 69% to 44% and 66% to 48% of each system's wrong answers, respectively. Crucially, evidence recovery does not produce a proportional reduction in total error: premature resolutions and abstentions increase as missing-evidence failures decrease. ai.title: Critical Minerals: BLM Should Ensure Individuals and Businesses Meet Citizenship Requirements for Hardrock Mining Claims
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found The Department of the Interior’s Bureau of Land Management (BLM) administers mining claims that grant the exclusive right to extract critical and other hardrock minerals from most federal lands. U.S. mining laws include citizenship requirements for individuals and business entities holding such claims, known as mining claimants. Under these laws, mining claimants generally must be U.S. citizens, which can include individuals as well as business entities incorporated in a U.S. state or territory. Foreign entities are not qualified to be claimants, but their subsidiaries can hold claims if they are incorporated in the U.S. Mining claimants are not required to disclose to BLM if they are a subsidiary of another entity, foreign or domestic, and they do not have to provide information on any foreign investment they may receive. Under BLM’s regulations and guidance, the agency collects basic identifying information from individuals and business entities holding mining claims. However, BLM generally does not collect citizenship information and does not document if mining claimants meet the U.S. citizenship requirements. In addition, BLM officials said the agency rarely verifies the citizenship of mining claimants. As a result, BLM generally does not know whether mining claimants are qualified to hold mining claims. ai.title: Critical Minerals: Limited Available Information on the Full Extent of Foreign Investment in Mining on Federal Lands
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found The U.S critical mineral supply chain faces numerous constraints, including the need for substantial capital investment and limited domestic processing capacity. The U.S. exports large quantities of domestically extracted ore to Canada, Mexico, and China, among other countries. Copper Mine on Federal Lands The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the Forest Service oversee hardrock mines on federal land. As of February 2026, there were 632 approved hardrock mining plans of operation on federal land. The 1872 Mining Law generally requires mining claimants to be U.S. citizens or business entities incorporated in the U.S. Foreign businesses can meet this requirement by having a U.S. subsidiary serve as the claimant. While there is limited available information on the full extent of foreign investment in mining on federal lands and parent-subsidiary relationships, GAO reviewed ownership information of 43 claimants and operators associated with critical mineral mines on federal lands. GAO determined ownership for 32 of those companies and found that 14 were subsidiaries of foreign entities. GAO found that none of the 14 had Chinese-owned parent companies, but in at least two cases, Chinese entities had financial interest in the foreign parent companies. ai.title: Artificial Intelligence: Actions and Opportunities to Implement Responsible Use in DOD
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in a variety of scenarios, or use cases, in the Department of Defense (DOD). In guidance, DOD established AI Ethical Principles and the concept of Responsible AI to ensure the safety and trustworthiness of AI systems. DOD further defined six tenets to guide Responsible AI implementation. Most of the 10 DOD components GAO surveyed reported taking at least initial steps to establish oversight and implement Responsible AI tenets in the selected surveyed use cases. The Office of the Chief Digital and AI Officer (CDAO), through its Responsible AI Division, established the Responsible AI Working Council as the working-level collaborative group for Responsible AI. However, CDAO officials said the council did not meet from late 2024 until August 2025. Officials from four DOD components told GAO they faced Responsible AI implementation challenges during this time that would have benefited from collaboration. Six of 10 surveyed components reported that sharing Responsible AI resources and best practices would benefit their implementation efforts. Although officials said the council resumed meetings in August 2025, it is at risk of lapsing again as it does not have a charter that defines roles and responsibilities and specifies meeting frequency. trade.raw_summary: 經濟部今（12）日召開貿易救濟審議會，會中就我國對越南特定冷軋不銹鋼扁軋鋼品反傾銷案之產業損害初步調查結果進行審議，認定有合理跡象顯示國內產業遭受實質損害。後續將移請財政部進行傾銷調查。 經濟部表示，本案調查資料涵蓋期間（112年1月至115年6月），越南特定冷軋不銹鋼扁軋鋼品進口量自113年至114年大幅增加，進口價格逐年下降，且皆低於國產品內銷價格。國產品為與之競爭不得不跟進減價，減價幅度更甚於涉案貨物，惟因內銷價格仍高於涉案傾銷貨物致流失客戶，即便我國需求有所成長時也不見改善，導致市場占有率持續下降及內銷虧損擴大，國內產業營運狀況持續惡化；至115年1-6月因申請人宣布即將申請反傾銷調查，加上價差縮小，國內產業各項經濟指標，包括內銷虧損情形始不致繼續惡化。顯示越南特定冷軋不銹鋼扁軋鋼品傾銷進口對國內產業造成不利影響。 依據「平衡稅及反傾銷稅課徵實施辦法」規定，我國反傾銷案件調查由財政部與經濟部分工，分別負責「傾銷」調查與「損害」調查。程序上先由經濟部進行產業損害初步調查，如認定成立，則移請財政部進行傾銷「初步」及「最後」調查，如其「最後」調查認定傾銷成立，再由經濟部進行產業損害「最後」調查，最終交由財政部決定是否課徵反傾銷稅。 經濟部將產業損害初步調查認定結果通知財政部後，財政部應於通知送達之翌日起70日內作成有無傾銷的初步認定，並決定是否臨時課徵反傾銷稅。 經濟部表示，本案如須進行產業損害「最後」調查，經濟部將就國內產業狀況進一步瞭解及查證，並蒐集各方針對課徵反傾銷稅對下游產業等國家整體經濟利益影響之意見，提供財政部關稅稅率審議小組參考。屆時並不排除其他任何新增不同事實與分析，而獲致不同的結論。 有關產業損害初步調查報告公開版可於今(115)年11月12日起至貿易署網站（網址：https://www.trade.gov.tw/）「經貿往來」/「我國採行之貿易救濟措施」/「案件調查」項下之「調查報告」下載。 貿易署發言人：胡副署長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7109、02-2397-7178、0966-525-106 業務聯絡人：綜合企劃組邱組長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7361

trade.raw_summary: 財政部 公告 發文日期：中華民國115年10月13日 發文字號：台財關字第1151027218號 附件： 主旨：力麟科技股份有限公司申請對自中國大陸產製進口特定聚醯胺薄膜課徵反傾銷稅、臨時課徵反傾銷稅及回溯課徵反傾銷稅案，經本部初步認定部分涉案廠商有傾銷情事，自115年10月19日起臨時課徵反傾銷稅。 依據：平衡稅及反傾銷稅課徵實施辦法（下稱實施辦法）第12條至第14條，及本部關稅稅率審議小組115年9月24日第72次會議決議。 公告事項： 一、本部關稅稅率審議小組第72次會議決議略以：本案依據經濟部產業損害初步調查結果，認定有合理跡象顯示，涉案傾銷進口產品對國內產業造成實質損害，且我國產業在調查期間將繼續遭受損害；復經本部初步調查認定部分涉案廠商有傾銷情事，爰依實施辦法第13條規定，對相關涉案廠商之涉案產品臨時課徵反傾銷稅，為期4個月。 二、本案臨時課徵反傾銷稅之範圍、對象、稅率及期間如下： (一)課徵範圍： １、貨品名稱：特定聚醯胺薄膜（Certain Polyamide Film）。 ２、貨品範圍：以重量計含超過50%之聚醯胺-6，不論其表面是否經印刷、塗覆以任何材料或進行任何表面處理，未切或已切成長方形，但未經進一步加工之薄膜或箔。 ３、貨品規格： (１)厚度：0.0114公厘（含）以上至0.0315公厘（含）以下。 (２)寬度：超過5公厘。 (３)排除項目：具下列任一成分或特性之薄膜，不屬涉案貨物： 甲、薄膜表面含有金屬成分者。 乙、攝氏20度至23度且相對溼度50%至65%之測試條件下，薄膜厚度為0.015公厘時，氧氣穿透率小於15mL/(m?·day·atm)，即小於15毫升/(每平方公尺·每日·1標準大氣壓的純氧)者。 ４、參考貨品分類號列：39209229105及39209229203。 ５、用途：應用於食品、化學用品、醫療（藥）用品與電子材料包裝等。 (二)課徵對象： １、輸出國或產製國：中國大陸。 ２、國外製造商及出口商：昆山運城塑業有限公司、運城其龍新材料有限公司、鶴山運城新材料有限公司、廈門長塑實業有限公司、福建長塑實業有限公司、滄州東鴻制膜科技有限公司、滄州東鴻包裝材料有限公司、重慶明珠塑料有限公司、德州東鴻新材料有限公司、蕪湖明珠制膜科技有限公司、曉星化纖（嘉興）有限公司及佛山佛塑科技集團股份有限公司。 ３、國內進口商：慕明企業有限公司、展仝企業有限公司、建?股份有限公司及光展應材股份有限公司。 ４、其他未列名之涉案貨物製造商、出口商或進口商。 (三)臨時課徵稅率： １、昆山運城塑業有限公司（製造商）、運城其龍新材料有限公司（關聯製造商）及鶴山運城新材料有限公司（關聯製造商）：0%。 ２、其他製造商或出口商：40.21%。 ３、前揭個別廠商之臨時課徵稅率，係依其於調查期間提供資料計算決定，故涉案貨物須由該等廠商於該國生產製造並直接出口至我國，始得適用。 (四)課徵期間：依據實施辦法第13條第3項規定，臨時課徵之反傾銷稅，其課徵期間最長為4個月；如經占涉案貿易額相當比例之國外出口商請求，得延長為6個月。 三、本案尚須進行傾銷最後調查，依實地查核結果或其他新事證，可能獲致不同之傾銷差率或作成不同結論。 四、本案後續調查程序：依據實施辦法第14條及第16條規定，本部初步認定之案件，應於初步認定公告之翌日起60日內完成有無傾銷之最後認定。經最後認定有傾銷事實者，本部應即通知經濟部。經濟部應於接獲通知之翌日起40日內，作成該傾銷是否損害我國產業之最後調查認定並通知本部。本部應於接獲經濟部通知之翌日起10日內，提交關稅稅率審議小

trade.title: Critical Minerals: Limited Available Information on the Full Extent of Foreign Investment in Mining on Federal Lands
trade.raw_summary: What GAO Found The U.S critical mineral supply chain faces numerous constraints, including the need for substantial capital investment and limited domestic processing capacity. The U.S. exports large quantities of domestically extracted ore to Canada, Mexico, and China, among other countries. Copper Mine on Federal Lands The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the Forest Service oversee hardrock mines on federal land. As of February 2026, there were 632 approved hardrock mining plans of operation on federal land. The 1872 Mining Law generally requires mining claimants to be U.S. citizens or business entities incorporated in the U.S. Foreign businesses can meet this requirement by having a U.S. subsidiary serve as the claimant. While there is limited available information on the full extent of foreign investment in mining on federal lands and parent-subsidiary relationships, GAO reviewed ownership information of 43 claimants and operators associated with critical mineral mines on federal lands. GAO determined ownership for 32 of those companies and found that 14 were subsidiaries of foreign entities. GAO found that none of the 14 had Chinese-owned parent companies, but in at least two cases, Chinese entities had financial interest in the foreign parent companies.
